https://www.lowkickmma.com/modestas-buka.text: Modestas Bukauskas turned the fight completely on its head at UFC Paris , surviving a dangerous opening round before rallying to stop Oumar Sy with a vicious second-round TKO. Sy appeared firmly in control early, using his kicks to create an opening for a takedown before taking Bukauskas down and unleashing a heavy barrage of ground-and-pound. The French light heavyweight nearly found the finish before the end of the opening frame, but Bukauskas managed to survive the onslaught and make it back to his corner. https://www.dw.com/en/latvia-votes-in-pa.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Ngfd Centrist Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (right) is the favorite, but his coalition is expected to emerge weakened Image: Wojtek Radwanski/AFP Advertisement Polls opened in Latvia on Saturday with some 1.5 million people eligible to vote in the country's 11th parliamentary election since independence from the Soviet Union in 1991. The election, which sees 100 seats in the Saeima being contested by 14 parties using a proportional system, has been dominated by rising living costs and national security concerns in the small Baltic country which borders both Russia and Belarus . Latvia's current prime minister, Andris Kulbergs, has only been in office since May after the previous government collapsed over a dispute about Ukrainian drones . His center-right, conservative United List alliance was leading in the polls ahead of the vote – but his coalition is expected to emerge weakened as populist parties gain. Latvia vote shaped by Russia fears To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Latvia vote shaped by Russia concerns Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine is seen as a direct threat to national security in Latvia which, like Ukraine, is a former Soviet state with a sizeable ethnic Russian and Russian-speaking minority. Unlike Ukraine , however, Latvia is a member of both the European Union and NATO . Riga is one of Kyiv's closest partners and supporters, having committed itself by law to spending at least 5% of GDP on defense – leaving less room for spending elsewhere. Many Latvians complain of high prices and low wages, the economy is sluggish, the health system is under strain, and emigration and an ageing population remain persistent challenges. Populist movements such as the Sovereign Power/Young Latvians Alliance and the Latvia First party have attempted to exploit discontent by taking a less stringent line towards Moscow and arguing that a complete economic decoupling from Russia is damaging. Lessons from Latvia: How to deal with Russian hybrid threats To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video German Eurofighter jets in Latvian airspace Nevertheless, no parties are proposing any major deviation from Latvia's clear foreign policy alignment with the EU and NATO. Indeed, four German Eurofighter jets have been deployed to protect Latvian airspace during the election in response to a request from Riga. Once ballots are counted, attention is likely to shift quickly to coalition negotiations, which could prove lengthy and complex. Partial results are expected on Saturday evening, with preliminary official results due on Sunday. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/08/sout.text: South Korea recalled its ambassador to Ukraine on Wednesday over Kyiv's public disclosure of the repatriation of two North Korean prisoners of war, in a continued public dispute between the two countries.Seoul's foreign ministry announced it was recalling ambassador Park Ki-chan, citing the unauthorised disclosure of information about the handover.The ministry said it hoped to resolve outstanding issues through continued consultations and that the South Korean embassy in Kyiv would remain open.The dispute began on 23 September, when Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated at the UN General Assembly that North Korean soldiers captured fighting on Russia's side had been repatriated.Seoul argues the disclosure endangered the soldiers' families in North Korea, where the regime is known to punish the relatives of defectors and those who fall into enemy hands.Ukraine rejected the accusations. Zelenskyy's adviser Dmytro Lytvyn said at the end of September that no confidentiality agreement existed."There was no such agreement, that is not true. And it would be wrong to conceal what happens to particular prisoners," he wrote on social media.Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha described it as a diplomatic misunderstanding and expressed hope for a swift resolution.South Korean President Lee Jae-myung had previously warned of "additional measures" if Kyiv did not acknowledge a breach of a confidentiality agreement and issue a public apology.On Tuesday, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Seoul had received an apology from Ukraine, but it fell short of what his country expected.Oil shipments to Russia a further complicationReports indicate that South Korean ports shipped more than 176,000 tonnes of fuel oil, mostly diesel, to Russia in July and August, based on port documents and vessel-tracking data published by The Guardian.Seven tankers, three of which are subject to UK and EU sanctions, made 14 voyages over the two-month period, according to reports.Vladyslav Vlasjuk, Ukraine's presidential envoy on sanctions policy, said the timing was no coincidence."These deliveries began precisely when Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries reduced processing volumes and caused a fuel shortage in the Russian Federation. In other words, imports from South Korea effectively helped Russia offset the consequences of losing its own refining capacity," he wrote on social media.Kyiv's reaction came despite Seoul joining the coalition of countries that imposed enhanced export controls on Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022.In 2024, South Korea expanded its list of controlled goods to more than 1,400 items and tightened restrictions on so-called Common High Priority Items, components Russia procures through third countries for use in missiles, drones and other weapons.Seoul has also sanctioned Russian ships, companies and individuals involved in military cooperation with North Korea.In response to reports, South Korea's foreign ministry said Seoul "supports and is actively participating in global efforts to end the war in Ukraine and restore peace."It declined to comment on specific shipments or the arrival of sanctioned vessels, saying the country strictly observes its own export-control measures against Russia.
